items.project_definition: A manual interaction step executed by a human operator within the browser interface to trigger a specific system behavior or state transition during the verification phase.
A cross-origin resource sharing security mechanism enforced by web browsers that necessitates serving project files through a local development host to prevent module loading failures.
The four foundational persistent storage mutation primitives applied to catalog entries, encompassing insertion, retrieval, modification, and removal operations within the management area.
The anticipated observable result or interface state transition that must occur immediately following a manual verification step, serving as the pass or fail criteria for the scenario.
A data typing rule dictating that monetary values assigned to catalog entries must be processed as non-floating decimal structures to prevent rounding errors during dynamic sorting operations.
The core client-side scripting language utilized without external frameworks, relying on native browser module systems to handle all dynamic rendering and local storage logic.
The designated integrated development environment extension providing a local live hosting server required to bypass browser cross-origin restrictions during the manual testing phase.
